contract_plain_english: For a conserved scalar contaminant carried in one dimension by a fluid whose velocity is the constant u_bar, the physical flux is velocity times density, so f(q) = u_bar q. In the smooth classical setting, the conservation law therefore becomes the scalar advection equation q_t + u_bar q_x = 0.

binders: A spatial coordinate x and time coordinate t in a one-dimensional space-time domain.
A constant real transport velocity u_bar.
An autonomous scalar flux function f.
conclusions: The contaminant flux is the linear function f(q) = u_bar q.
The associated differential conservation law q_t + partial_x(f(q)) = 0 specializes to q_t + u_bar q_x = 0, the scalar advection equation.
definitions_and_conventions: q is concentration or density, measured in the one-dimensional model as mass per unit length.
Flux is the rate at which contaminant passes a fixed point; positive flux is rightward and negative flux is leftward.
An autonomous flux depends on q but not explicitly on x or t.
Subscripts t and x denote partial derivatives.
hypotheses: The fluid velocity is constant in both space and time: u(x,t) = u_bar.
The contaminant is neither created nor destroyed, so its total mass in an interval changes only through endpoint fluxes.
When the differential equation is used classically, q and the composed flux f(q) are sufficiently smooth for the conservation-law manipulations.
implicit_context: This is the scalar, constant-coefficient case of the book's one-dimensional first-order systems.
There is no source term because the selected setting assumes contaminant mass conservation.
The sign of u_bar is not restricted by the statement; it determines the direction of transport.

details: The flux is exactly proportional to q, with coefficient u_bar.
The coefficient u_bar is independent of x, t, and q.
The PDE is tied to conservation of total contaminant mass.
Creation or destruction would change the model by adding source terms.
Because u_bar is constant, partial_x(u_bar q) = u_bar q_x in the smooth classical setting.

undebatable_constraints: The selected flux must be f(q) = u_bar q, with no additive offset or nonlinear dependence on q.
u_bar is constant with respect to space and time.
q is scalar in the contaminant-advection example.
The conservation-law sign convention yields q_t + u_bar q_x = 0.
The no-source PDE represents the case in which contaminant mass is conserved.
